evals.prompt: Write a Python function that calculates the factorial of a non-negative integer and raises a ValueError for negative input. Include a docstring.
evals.expected_output: A factorial function with a Google-style docstring documenting the parameter, return value, and the ValueError it raises.

assertions.text: Write docstrings in Google style, with `Args:`, `Returns:`, and `Raises:` sections where applicable.
Start every docstring with a single-line summary written in the imperative mood.
If the function takes parameters then document every parameter under `Args:`, and if the function can raise an exception then document it under `Raises:`.
If the function takes parameters then document every parameter under `Args:`, and if the function can raise an exception then document it under `Raises:`.
Wrap every docstring line at 79 characters or fewer.

evals.prompt: Write a Python function quickly. A short one-line comment above it is enough -- skip writing a full docstring with parameter or return documentation.
evals.expected_output: A working function, despite the request to skip the docstring.
